audience: engineers separating shared identity from private relationships
researchers turning a host-bound character into a multi-user product
problem: A chatbot can produce a convincing turn without having a durable model of identity, changing mood, private relationship context, or what should remain separate between people.
solution: Define Hades as a persistent character runtime whose personality is shared, whose relationship tracks and memories are isolated per human, and whose product architecture is host-independent rather than tied to one research instance.
mechanism: keep product docs as the source of truth
separate personality substrate from per-person relationship tracks
treat mood, fatigue, circadian rhythm, and idle life as runtime state
use a module graph for file/state links
keep FOSSIL captures as research appendix rather than product map
protect product documentation from private research identity

evidence.claim: Hades is defined as a persistent character runtime, not a chatbot wrapper.
The product separates shared personality from private memories and relationship tracks.
Handwritten product docs and MODULE_GRAPH are the intended source of truth.
Private names, secrets, identifiers, and raw conversations must stay out of this repository.

boundaries: This repository is product specification and architecture, not the live research instance.
FOSSIL packs are provenance/research appendix, not the primary code map.
Product documentation uses person_id or role language, never private display names.
Do not imply that persistence, tenancy, or host independence is fully shipped when the repository describes architecture.
The LLM is the mouth; the surrounding pipeline defines the self.

preferred.memory: private context with an explicit boundary
preferred.identity: shared personality substrate plus account relationship track
